title: What is Middleware?

tableData.title: Capabilities of Middleware
rows: Logging the time every request comes in.
Parsing a JWT and attaching the `user` to `req.user`.
Sending a 401 Unauthorized response if a user is not logged in.
Calling `next()` so the actual route handler can do its job.

definition: Middleware functions are functions that have access to the request object (`req`), the response object (`res`), and the `next` function in the application's request-response cycle. Middleware can execute any code, make changes to the req/res objects, end the response cycle, or call `next()` to pass control to the next middleware in line.

answers.answer: Middleware functions are functions that have access to the request object (`req`), the response object (`res`), and the `next` function in the application's request-response cycle.

answers.question: When should you avoid using What is Middleware??
answers.answer: It depends on the specific architectural requirements and performance bottlenecks of your application. Overusing it can sometimes lead to tightly coupled code.
